knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunkbase 3110) with the modular input for `azure:monitor:resource`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `ResourceId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics export to Event Hub; map metrics in Microsoft Cloud Services add-on.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:resource" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:resource" operationName="Microsoft.*Availability Drop"
| table _time ResourceId metricName total average
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.102_azure_storage_account_av_102"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:resource` in `index=azure` to detect azure storage account availability drop. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Azure portal Metrics explorer for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `ResourceId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_102_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Timechart, single-value SLA breach, top resources table..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (`Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunkbase 3110) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure storage account availability drop so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
